historical_record.description: Westside Courts opened in the spring of 1943 with 136 units — four L-shaped and two U-shaped three-storey buildings arranged symmetrically around courtyards holding open space, drying yards and small play areas, with moulded concrete exterior stairs. Lester Hurd and James J. Mitchell designed it, and a 1946 survey of the city's public housing called it the most unusual and interesting design of any San Francisco Housing Authority project. It was the first public housing in the city made available to African Americans. Beniamino Bufano's granite St. Francis on Horseback, carved in 1935, was installed here in 1945.

Westside Courts, a public housing project built in 1943 and open to African Americans under the Housing Authority's neighbourhood-pattern policy because the surrounding area already had a Black majority. A Bufano sculpture stood in its central courtyard. It has since been rehabilitated inside and out by the San Francisco Housing Development Corporation.
